comparison: Both strongly support the core finding that genome copy number affects growth rate (C26-C34). OpenEval provides detailed technical evaluation of methods and potential artifacts, while peer reviewers emphasize the novelty of rapid effects and compelling experimental evidence. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED with high confidence.

Perfect agreement on ribosome concentration findings (C41-C44). Both evaluations confirm that ribosomal protein concentration remains constant across cell sizes, ruling out ribosome concentration as the limiting factor. OpenEval notes methodological strengths (two independent methods), while peer reviewers accept without challenge. Both SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on ribosome activity findings (C47-C57). Both support that ribosome activity decreases in 1N cells and correlates with growth rate. OpenEval provides detailed technical evaluation of single-molecule tracking methods, while peer reviewers emphasize the compelling combination of experiment and modeling. Both SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on RNAP findings (C60-C71). Both support that RNAP concentration increases while activity plateaus in 1N cells. OpenEval provides detailed methodological evaluation, while peer reviewers accept this as key evidence for DNA limitation mechanism. Both SUPPORTED.
Both support the Rsd control experiment (C72-C73). OpenEval includes this within broader RNAP analysis, while peer reviewers explicitly note this control rules out Rsd involvement. Both SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on differential RNA decay findings (C75-C81). Both support that mRNA decays faster than rRNA in 1N cells. OpenEval provides detailed technical evaluation of fluorescent probe methods and acknowledges interpretive limitations, while peer reviewers accept as supporting evidence without challenge. Both SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on modeling results (C85-C92). Both support that ODE models successfully recapitulate experimental data. OpenEval notes phenomenological nature and parameter fitting concerns, while peer reviewers emphasize compelling combination of experiment and modeling. Both SUPPORTED.

Agreement on medium-dependent effects (C93-C96, C133-C134). Both support that RNAP effects are rapid across media while ribosome/growth effects are delayed in some media. OpenEval notes comprehensive data, peer reviewers accept without challenge. Both SUPPORTED.

Both address buffering mechanisms (C97, C132, C135-C136), but with different confidence levels. OpenEval marks these as SUPPORTED but notes speculation, while peer reviewers explicitly classify as UNCERTAIN and recognize as hypothesis for future work rather than demonstrated finding.

Strong agreement on global proteome remodeling (C98-C102, C8, C10). Both support that ~60% of proteins show concentration changes in 1N cells. OpenEval notes technical details about sample purity, while peer reviewers emphasize this as a surprising key finding. Both SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on mRNA-protein correlation (C103-C104, C141). Both support the strong correlation (ρ=0.76) demonstrating proteome changes are driven by mRNA changes. OpenEval provides detailed statistical evaluation, peer reviewers explicitly state changes stem from mRNA levels. Both SUPPORTED.

Agreement on mRNA decay rate correlation (C107-C108, C142). Both support the modest but significant correlation with mRNA decay rates. OpenEval notes weak correlation and acknowledges uncertainty, peer reviewers highlight unstable transcripts being more affected as a surprising finding. Both SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on essential gene prioritization (C109-C110, C143-C144). Both support that essential genes show superscaling behavior. OpenEval notes strong statistical significance but questions mechanism, peer reviewers highlight as key finding suggesting buffering mechanisms. Both SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on C. crescentus validation (C40, C112-C113). Both support cross-species conservation. OpenEval notes limited extent of C. crescentus data and questions broad conservation claim based on two species, while peer reviewers emphasize importance of distant species confirmation. Both SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on DNA dilution threshold (C118-C121). Both support that cells are sensitive to small DNA dilutions and live at the cusp of limitation. OpenEval notes uncertainty in crude estimations, peer reviewers emphasize rapid effects and fine balance of bacterial physiology. Both SUPPORTED.

Perfect agreement on stress response controls (C36). Both support that SOS and stringent responses are not responsible for growth defects. OpenEval notes these strengthen DNA limitation interpretation, peer reviewers explicitly confirm independence from stress pathways. Both SUPPORTED.

Agreement on dose-response relationship (C37-C39). OpenEval includes these claims within broader growth rate analysis (R1), while peer reviewers treat as separate confirmatory evidence. Both support the nucleoid number-growth rate relationship. Both SUPPORTED.

Overlap on high-level conclusions (C3-C5, C9). OpenEval R17 evaluates abstract summary statements as supported by detailed evidence, while peer R1 evaluates core experimental findings. Both address same conclusions from different levels of detail. Both SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on summary claims (C8, C10). OpenEval R17 evaluates abstract statements about proteome remodeling, while peer R11 evaluates detailed proteome data. Both support proteome changes but from different analytical perspectives. Both SUPPORTED.

Agreement on eukaryotic parallels (C11). Both support comparisons with eukaryotic studies strengthen significance. OpenEval notes limited evidence for broad conservation claim, peer reviewers accept cross-domain comparisons. Both SUPPORTED.

OpenEval evaluates oriC proximity correlation (C145-C146) as SUPPORTED but notes weak correlation (ρ=0.23) and unclear biological significance. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; this subtle post-transcriptional finding may not have been highlighted in peer reviews.

OpenEval evaluates background knowledge claims (C1-C2, C12-C25) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. These are contextual claims establishing field knowledge rather than new findings, so peer reviewers did not separately evaluate them.

OpenEval evaluates speculative claims about future directions (C125-C132, C153-C154) as UNCERTAIN, appropriately noting these are hypotheses not tested in current study. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate these discussion points, though R10 touches on buffering speculation.

OpenEval evaluates established knowledge and logical reasoning supporting experimental design (C45, C58-C59) as SUPPORTED. These methodological justifications were not separately evaluated by peer reviewers.

OpenEval evaluates additional protein class characterization (C147-C151) as SUPPORTED, including GO term analysis and nucleoid-associated proteins. These descriptive findings were not separately highlighted in peer review evaluations.
